bear_case: Ceilings look large ($150M Owl, $239M GDMS, $89M PMAT, $998M Trace) but obligations at award were $10K, $25.7M and $23K; DISA CDES procurement lines are ~$1-2M/yr; the money is in sustainment services and program integration, not licences. Low-to-high promotion is absorbed by Platform One and factory budgets (free to programs). The BICES-MPE bridge has no vendor budget line - it is a NATO BGX / DISA accreditation and policy decision. Exercise-only evidence (WFX, Balikatan, Bold Quest) shows pain but purgatory: coalition data-centric security has been 'demonstrated and assessed' annually since 2022 without a program of record. Consultancy drift is the realistic outcome for any small entrant.
strongest_single_argument: No budget line exists that a new, unlisted vendor can be paid from: AC-4(20) forbids using unlisted CDS, and the listed vendors hold sole-source vehicles through 2029-2030.
what_would_change_my_mind: A competed (not sole-source) DoD solicitation for automated low-to-high promotion or a software-defined tactical CDS explicitly open to non-listed vendors with a funded transition line, or a DISA/J6 program of record for a BICES-MPE bridge that buys commercial software.
narrower_survivable_version: None as a company; subcontract filter/evidence content to a listed vendor.

bear_case: Incumbents already have it. Owl holds the only listed voice/video/FMV guards and a $150M-ceiling Phase III IDIQ and authors DFDL; GDMS holds TACDS and the BICES TNE CDS IDIQ; Everfox, Lockheed (Radiant Mercury) and Northrop hold enterprise and program guards; Defense Unicorns (Zarf/UDS, $136M Series B, Jan 2026) owns air-gap and one-way low-to-high delivery; Second Front and Palantir (PFCS Forward IL6) own classified hosting; Platform One Secret is government-owned and free. Every interface - NSA assessment, filter SDKs, high-side registries, classified eMASS, DISA MPE - is controlled by government or a listed vendor. Switching cost for programs is a re-accreditation, so nobody switches. Government-owned software (Platform One, Big Bang, Zarf) already covers the unclassified layer for free.
strongest_single_argument: The only unclassified surface a startup could build on is open source or vendor-owned, so any useful contribution is absorbed at zero cost by the listed vendor that controls the interface and the sole-source vehicle.
what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that NCDSMO or DISA is opening a software-defined, vendor-neutral filter framework where third parties can publish assessed filter content independently of the guard vendor, with a payment mechanism.
narrower_survivable_version: Open-source contribution to Zarf/UDS/OpenTDF for credibility only; not a business.

bear_case: Classification dependence is immediate: real filter specs, ATO packages and BICES/MPE product formats are gated. The product cannot be demonstrated credibly without classified access, an NCDSMO-listed guard and an authorizing official. NCDSMO listing takes years; CDS are export-controlled (RTB covers CDS sold for export); FOCI (32 CFR 117.11) treats the non-citizen owners as foreign interests; personnel clearances require U.S. citizenship, so the Indonesian founder can never work on the core and the German founder not for years; SBIR's >50% U.S.-citizen/PR ownership test fails a 50/50 split. A credible military demo costs $3-8M (cleared staff, FCL, sponsor) versus $250k available; the $50-150k MVP proves nothing an AO or CDS buyer needs. Procurement to a first program insertion is a 3-5 year path (Owl SBIR II to Phase III; PMAT prototype OT to production OT). All of this needs export-control and security counsel, but no plausible legal structure makes the founders able to do the work.
strongest_single_argument: The founding team cannot legally or practically work on the product's core, and the parts they can work on are open source.
what_would_change_my_mind: Both founders become U.S. citizens with clearances and recruit a cleared CDS engineer with prior NCDSMO assessment experience plus $10M+ of patient capital - at which point it is a different company and team.
narrower_survivable_version: None for this team; redirect effort to unclassified DevSecOps evidence tooling (G2-type gaps) where the same policy tailwinds apply without the classification gate.
